metadata.title: The Sovereign Dual-Substrate Architecture: Governed Execution, Automated Falsification, and Quantum Hardware Control on Constrained Consumer Silicon (Release v4.8.0)
metadata.description:
OSIRIS v4.8.0 Monograph & Governed Release Package

This release encapsulates the sovereign architecture, operational history, and empirical verification of the OSIRIS and dna::}{::lang project, featuring the complete prospective quantum control campaign on IBM Heron r2 hardware (ibm_marrakesh) and the resolution of the OSIRIS vs. Qiskit dynamical decoupling benchmark.

Key Empirical & Architectural Additions in v4.8.0:

  • Resolution of the OSIRIS vs. Qiskit Ideal Benchmark: Established through 3-engine numerical simulation (analytical toggling frame, SciPy matrix exponentiation, and Qiskit Aer) that ideal commuting ZZ crosstalk cancellation is governed by toggling-frame exposure bisection (A_uv = 0). Proved that Qiskit configured with matched sublattice staggering achieves identical perfect refocusing (agreement within 3.93e-7 Aer / 1.58e-12 ODE), confirming that the advantage lies in hardware-aware scheduling policies rather than SDK-level limitations.
  • Forensic Post-Mortem of Prospective Experiment E2: Documented the empirical falsification of Adaptive Scheduler v1.0 on 4 held-out couplers, identifying that single-qubit maximum dephasing thresholds improperly defaulted to synchronous control, while bilateral partner dephasing governs CPMG breakdown. Cluster-robust inference (G=4, df=3) demonstrated that Fixed 80ns stagger outperformed synchronous XY8 by +0.446 +- 0.113 pp (p_2s = 0.0289).
  • OSIRIS Control Compiler v2 (Risk-Aware Graph Surrogate): Formulated a cost-sensitive objective J(s) = F_hat(s) - lambda*sigma_F(s) - gamma*C(s). In open-system Lindblad master equation benchmarks across all 14 ibm_marrakesh couplers (28 cells with finite pulse width tau_p = 36ns, detuning, T1/T2, and filter leakage), OSIRIS v2 achieved +1.825 pp over Fixed 80ns (p_2s = 0.0004) and +2.356 pp over synchronous XY8 (p_2s = 0.0069). On a connected 5-qubit heavy-hex chain (Q12-Q19), shifting only the central vertex Q15 beat uniform staggering by +2.24 pp.
  • Prospective Physical Hardware Validation (Experiment E3 Pilot): Executed under SYS-021 Ledger Block #15 on ibm_marrakesh (Job dbm00gd8mdtc73d6vjcg, 216 ISA circuits, 221,184 physical shots across 3 unseen physical couplers), OSIRIS Control Compiler v2 achieved 78.529% mean Bell-state fidelity, beating the primary Fixed 80ns baseline (77.878%) by +0.651 pp (block-clustered p_1s = 0.0348, positive in all 3 blocks) and beating synchronous XY8 (78.003%) by +0.526 pp (p_2s = 0.0454, positive in all 3 blocks).
  • Compiler Performance Benchmark: Across 5 heavy-hex workloads (2 to 12 qubits), OSIRIS delivered 6.80x mean compilation speedup vs. Qiskit Opt-1 + PadDynamicalDecoupling, 13.87x speedup and 3.71x lower memory vs. Qiskit Opt-3 + Staggered PadDynamicalDecoupling, with verified exact unitary preservation (|1 - F_Statevector| <= 3.3e-15).

The release bundle includes the complete Monograph with Amendment 3, compiled PDFs, executable benchmark suites, staged QPY archives, raw QPU bitstring counts, and cryptographic authorization receipts.
